content.title: About
content.content: Full Throttle is an energy drink designed to boost physical and mental performance. It contains caffeine, taurine, B‑vitamins, and sugar (or sugar substitutes in the diet version). Available in flavors such as "Pomegranate", "Apple‑Cinnamon" and "Strawberry‑Lemon".

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Full Throttle was first launched in 2005 as part of Monster Beverage's product line.
The brand markets itself as "for those who live at full speed" and frequently sponsors extreme sports events.
The formula includes taurine, an amino acid commonly used in energy drinks to support the nervous system.
In some markets a sugar‑free version is sold, sweetened with sucralose and acesulfame‑K.
The label typically lists caffeine content at 160 mg per 473 ml can.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, increasing alertness and reducing perceived fatigue.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: B‑vitamins help convert food into usable energy, supporting a more efficient metabolism.

items.title: Improved focus
items.content: Taurine may aid cognitive function and reaction time during high‑intensity activities.

items.title: Excess caffeine intake
items.content: High caffeine doses can cause anxiety, insomnia, rapid heartbeat, and elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sugared versions can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries if consumed frequently.

items.title: Not for children or pregnant women
items.content: Due to its high caffeine level, the drink is not recommended for children, adolescents, pregnant or nursing women.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Drink Full Throttle chilled, straight from the can. Limit consumption to 1‑2 cans per day. Do not mix with alcohol.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days for best quality.
